The ask

Referrals don't scale a boutique search firm

Philippe runs a retained-search practice built on decades of personal relationships in the European food industry — Managing Director, CFO, Head of Quality and senior commercial mandates for manufacturers across Germany, France, Poland and the Netherlands. That network wins mandates. It doesn't put new client companies in front of him on a schedule he controls. The brief: reach decision-makers at qualifying companies — 300 to 2,000+ employees, food and adjacent sectors, DACH/France/Benelux as the core market, UK excluded — without turning Philippe himself into a full-time prospector.

What we built

A signal layer under the cold email, not a mail-merge

Two things feed each other here. First, a signal layer: company news and hiring activity gets pulled from the open web (via Exa AI) and from five niche job boards per country — LinkedIn, Cadremploi, Xing, Indeed, Stepstone — then filtered against Philippe's actual ICP before anything gets touched by a human. Second, the outreach itself runs on two channels at once: cold email, and a LinkedIn sequencer connected to Philippe's own LinkedIn account, writing in his voice, triggered by the same signals — so a company expanding into a new market gets a message referencing that expansion, not a generic template. Every target's own site and careers pages also get scraped — in German, French and Dutch, not just English — so segmentation is based on what's actually happening at the company, not a guess from headcount.

The evidence

Seven exhibits, redacted where it matters

Exhibit A — A narrow market, mapped close to fully

Retained executive search in European food & ingredients is not a large addressable market. Rather than treat that as a limitation, the list was built to exhaust it: 1,151 qualifying companies (300–2,000+ employees, DACH/France/Benelux, food and adjacent sectors) and 2,064 contacts inside them — company and contact identities masked below, numbers are real.

Exhibit B — Deliverability held through August

Infra was picked on purpose, not by default: the recipient mix skews heavily corporate — Microsoft-domain inboxes — so sending leaned on Outlook (which delivers well into Microsoft) plus a custom SMTP block warmed for two months beforehand, which ended up outperforming Outlook on reputation.

August is EU vacation season — most of the reply volume is out-of-office autoresponders, not people. Shown honestly, split from genuine engagement, and broken down by sending infrastructure to confirm nothing was quietly getting blocked.

What the live dashboard looks like for one of these sending weeks — not a cherry-picked best week, just what a normal week in the campaign reads like.

The read

Not a closed case study — a live one

This isn't a wrapped-up success story with a final invoice. It's a cold list, in a language-fragmented market, for a search discipline — retained executive search, not contingency staffing — that most cold-email operators have never sold into. Two campaigns in, with a signal-and-segmentation layer built specifically for this vertical, the pipeline is still producing positive replies on sends going out this week, not coasting on one list pull from months ago.

Sends are still going out and replies are still coming in — this page reflects where the pipeline stands, not a fixed snapshot from a single push.
